subject: Finovate — telemetry compact export & header propagation ask
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finovate — telemetry compact export & header propagation ask

Team — looping you in on a hard requirement from Finovate (see attached SOW). They are close to signing but are asking for two small, high-priority platform capabilities before pilot kickoff: 

1) Compact, exportable per-request telemetry snapshot (compressed CSV) that includes propagated headers: tenant_id, trace_id, user_agent, route_tag. Must be tamper-evident (SHA256 hash per file) and delivered as a presigned S3 URL.

2) A small API to request an on-demand 7-day rolling snapshot (historical window) — they will use this for monthly audits. Snapshot should be produced within 30 minutes of request during business hours.

Bonus ask: ability to pin a request-level "residency_tag" so traffic for that tenant routes to NA nodes (compliance posture) — they understand this can be soft (routing preference) rather than strict at first.

Finovate attached a traffic sample (traffic_sample_log.gz) and their SOW (Finovate_SOW_v2.pdf). They expect these items to be in the commitment before signature; timeline they shared: pilot start by 2026-05-01, contract signature targeted this week pending feasibility.

Can you provide: 
- Minimal viable spec we can present (fields, format, retention semantics)
- High-level estimate (T-shirt and weeks) and risk items
- If we cannot deliver full residency pinning, what's a short-term fallback we can offer?

I can move this forward with legal/procurement once we have internal feasibility. Appreciate quick triage — Finovate is a strategic logos-win (deal FIN-3421).

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[karthik@redwood.com]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finovate — telemetry compact export & header propagation ask

Thanks Karthik — this helps. A few clarifying questions before we scope: 

• Delivery path: do they require exports to land in their S3 (preferred) or can we provide a signed temporary download? You mentioned presigned S3 URL — confirm if they own the bucket and KMS key.
• Schema: please confirm minimal set of columns they need. You listed tenant_id/trace_id/user_agent/route_tag — do they also need timestamp, model_name, token_count, request_payload_hash?
• Audit requirements: when you say tamper-evident, do they require a signed manifest with a KMS-backed signature or is a SHA256 file hash sufficient?
• Residency: is the requirement for a per-request routing preference or full tenant residency (i.e., all traffic for tenant stays in NA)?

Can you drop the HubSpot deal link and the SOW in the thread so I can attach to the PRD? Also flag if this is a must-have for signature (yes/no).

If this is a must-have, we can look at a narrow MLP: 1) export generator using our existing telemetry pipeline, 2) simple header propagation toggle (boolean) that requests opt-in to include tenant headers in export, 3) on-demand job runner producing a zipped CSV to presigned URL. We need engineering capacity; tagging as priority will require a resource allocation decision.

– Monica
Principal PM, Platform

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Nate Johnson <nate.johnson@finovate.com>, procurement@finovate.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finovate — telemetry compact export & header propagation ask

Monica — quick answers from the customer: 

• Delivery path: Finovate will host the S3 bucket and provide a KMS key. They expect us to generate a presigned PUT to their bucket for the snapshot.
• Schema: required columns: timestamp_iso, tenant_id, trace_id, route_tag, model_name, latency_ms, token_count, prompt_hash, response_status. (They said user_agent is optional.)
• Tamper evidence: they require a per-file SHA256 and a signed manifest — KMS-based signature preferred. They can accept a manifest signed by Redwood's KMS (we discussed previously during SOC2 review).
• Residency: Phase 1 = routing preference (soft pin to NA), Phase 2 = tenant residency (hard pin) may be contractual later. Phase 1 is a must for compliance review before pilot.

They explicitly flagged this as a gating item for signature. If we cannot commit to Phase 1 routing preference + export API, they will push signature out.

Attached again: Finovate_SOW_v2.pdf and traffic_sample_log.gz. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FIN-3421

Karthik

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2026 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finovate — telemetry compact export & header propagation ask

Thanks for the details. Quick engineering read: feasible as an MLP with reuse of our export pipeline and job runner. Proposed approach and risks below.

MVP approach (goal: minimal scope to unblock contract):
1) Header propagation: add a request-level flag that copies tenant_id and trace_id into the telemetry stream and ensures they are present in the export schema. Implementation: 1 week to add header plumbing + tests.
2) Export job: extend existing telemetry job to accept a time window and produce a gzip CSV snapshot to a presigned S3 PUT URL (customer-owned bucket). Implementation: 2–3 weeks (includes security review for presign flows and KMS handshake).
3) Manifest & tamper-evidence: compute SHA256 per-file and produce manifest.json; sign manifest with our KMS (envelope sign) — 1 week, needs security review.
4) Residency tag: routing preference flag at request-level — early rollout as soft preference (no hard guarantees) using existing smart-routing weight adjustment. Implementation: 2 weeks to wire flags + rollout gating.

Estimate: ~6 weeks (3 sprints) with 2 backend engineers + 1 infra engineer part-time. T-shirt: M (3–6 weeks).

Risks/Non-goals: 
• Hard tenant residency (guaranteed NA-only hosting) is NOT in MLP — that requires dedicated capacity and infra changes (estimate additional 6–10 weeks).
• Storage / cost: frequent ad-hoc snapshots could increase egress costs; we should limit on-demand snapshot frequency or charge for snapshots.
• Compliance sign-off: KMS signing flow requires security review and could add a week if there are integration blockers with customer KMS.

Ask from sales/product: 
• Approval to allocate 2 backend engineers for the next 6 weeks (we can start immediately if we greenlight).
• Product decision on snapshot SLAs (30 mins) and rate limits (e.g., 4 snapshots per tenant per month).
• Confirmation that Finovate will provide S3 bucket + KMS key.

If you want, I can draft an internal RFC and rough PRD this week; will need legal loop for manifest signing language in the SOW.

— Dev
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
